dish.title: Red Snapper a la Veracruzana with White Rice
dish.description: Red snapper fillets simmered in a Veracruz-style tomato sauce with green olives, capers, pickled jalapeños, garlic, bay, and oregano. Served with white rice and lime.

recipe_version.title: Red Snapper a la Veracruzana with White Rice
recipe_version.description: Red snapper fillets simmered in a Veracruz-style tomato sauce with green olives, capers, pickled jalapeños, garlic, bay, and oregano. Served with white rice and lime.

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: 1/2 tsp fish, 1/2 tsp sauce, 1/2 tsp rice

steps.title: Prep
steps.body: Chop the tomatoes, slice the onion and garlic, halve the olives, and rinse the capers and rice. Season the fish on both sides with 1/2 tsp salt. Chop the parsley and cut the limes into wedges.

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.body: Combine the rice, 2 1/4 cups water, and 1/2 tsp salt in a 2-quart saucepan. Bring to a boil over high heat, cover, turn to low, and cook 15 minutes; then rest covered off the heat 10 minutes. This runs inside steps 3 to 5 (overlap stated).

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.body: Heat the olive oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium. Cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes; add the garlic for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes, bay leaves, oregano, and 1/2 tsp salt and simmer, stirring, until the tomatoes collapse into a chunky sauce, about 8 minutes.

steps.title: Add the briny trio
steps.body: Stir in the olives, capers, and pickled jalapeños and simmer 2 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer the fish
steps.body: Nestle the fillets skin side down into the sauce and spoon sauce over the tops. Cover and simmer over medium-low until the fish is opaque, flakes, and reads 145 F, about 8 minutes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Remove the bay leaves. Fluff the rice, plate a fillet with plenty of sauce beside it, and finish with parsley and lime wedges.

coverage_contribution: First Mexican fish main that is not a taco (crispy-fish-tacos-cabbage-slaw is the only other Mexican fish dish). Red snapper as a fillet in sauce. HH001 fish dinner with no frying.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with crispy-fish-tacos-cabbage-slaw: no batter, no tortillas. Compared with grilled-swordfish-olive-caper: simmered in a tomato sauce, not grilled with a relish. Compared with garlic-tomato-mussels: finfish fillets, briny Veracruz sauce, rice not bread. Compared with filipino-fish-sinigang: thick tomato sauce, not sour broth. Compared with herbed-polenta-tomato-stew: a fish main in a briny sauce, not a vegetable stew over polenta.
not_duplicate_of: Not Italian acqua pazza or Moroccan fish tagine (no potatoes, no chermoula).
